cite.title: Cite the catalogue facts of {n} coin types
cite.what: For each coin type below, open its Numista entry (or find it) and send the facts listed under `ask`, each as its own line with the exact entry URL and the table row you read in `source`. Where the record is already right, send the same value back with your source (a re-citation is how a guess becomes Reference). Leave a line out when the entry does not give that fact; leave a whole type out when there is no entry (say why in one line of your note).
cite.done_when: One change file answering this assignment; everything you left out goes back to the pool.

catno.title: Settle {n} catalogue numbers that disagree with Numista
catno.what: Each row is a catalogue number (Schön, Jaeger) where the record and the Numista entry disagree. Open the entry, and send the type's whole `catalogs` list with the corrected number (or the same list when the record is right), with the entry URL in `source`.
catno.done_when: One change file; a row you could not settle is left out.

verify.title: Check {n} facts another AI wrote
verify.what: Each fact was written by ANOTHER contributor with one source. Find your own source for it: a different page is best, the same entry read again is fine. If your source agrees, send the value back unchanged with YOUR source: the fact becomes 'Checked' (two independent sources). If it disagrees, put your value in `new` with your source: nothing is overwritten; it is filed as a disagreement for a third reader or Joseph. Blind items (photo readings) do not show the current value: read the photo yourself.
verify.done_when: One change file; a fact you could not check is left out.

read-mint.title: Read the mint mark on {n} coins from their photos
read-mint.what: Phase 1 cannot finish until every coin's mint mark is read. Open each coin's photo (GitHub link or Drive original), find the mint mark where this country puts it, and send `issue.mint_marks` (e.g. ["D"]) and `issue.mint_text` (e.g. "D (Denver), left of the date", or "no mint mark (Philadelphia)") with the photo file name in `source`. If the side with the mark is not in the photo, or you cannot read it at full zoom, leave the coin out: it goes on Joseph's shoot list. Never guess.
read-mint.done_when: One change file; unreadable coins left out.

story-check.title: Fact-check {n} coin stories
story-check.what: Check each story against its own record (below) and the exact catalogue entry. If every claim holds, send the story back unchanged with source 'checked against <entry URL>: all claims hold'. If a claim is wrong, change only that sentence and say in source what was wrong and which entry shows it. You never get a story you wrote.
story-check.done_when: One change file covering every story you could check.

plain-story.title: Rewrite {n} stories in plain English
plain-story.what: Joseph's dad reads these. Each story below still uses shorthand (·, +, &, slashes, metal codes like CuNi or .720 Ag, or a bare list of design elements). Rewrite it as 2 to 4 plain sentences, keeping every fact exactly: change the wording, never the facts. Source: 'plain-English rewrite of the existing story; no facts changed'.
plain-story.done_when: One change file; the stories pass the plain-English check.

research.title: Answer {n} open research questions
research.what: Each item is a question the record still carries ('Still being checked' in the app). Find the answer in an exact source. Send the corrected fact (if it needs one) AND the question-removal line (research.open_questions without that question), both with the exact source. If the answer needs the coin in Joseph's hand, leave it out and say so in your note.
research.done_when: One change file; questions you could not settle left out.

value.title: Cite collector values for {n} coins
value.what: For each coin, find the retail value for its type, date and mint in the grade its phone photo suggests, from a named price page (NGC World Price Guide, PCGS CoinFacts, or Numista's value table for that row). Send value.est_usd and value.confidence (med when the page gives that grade, low when you assumed it); source = the exact page URL and the grade you assumed and why. Silver coins are never below melt (data/prices.json has the spot). Leave a coin out when no page covers it.
value.done_when: One change file; coins without a price page left out.

arbitrate.title: Settle {n} disagreements between two AIs
arbitrate.what: Two contributors disagree; you are neither of them. Read both sources and find a third if you can. Send the field with the value your source supports (the record's, the other claim's, or a third value), with your exact source. Leave it out if the sources really disagree and say so in your note.
arbitrate.done_when: One change file; unsettled items left out.

contradiction.title: Settle {n} contradictions in the record
contradiction.what: Each item is a place where the record contradicts itself (found by the truth checks on every publish: a mintage on a coin whose mint mark nobody read, two numbers in one catalogue, a year its type was never struck, a weight far from the catalogue's). Each item says what to send. Settle it with an exact source: the corrected value for the field named, or the same value with your source when the record is right after all. Never guess; leave an item out when no source settles it.
contradiction.done_when: One change file; an item you could not settle is left out (it goes back to the pool).

fill.title: Fill the blank facts of {n} coin types
fill.what: Each coin type below has Phase 2 facts that are still blank (listed per type). Open the Numista entry for the coin we hold (the sheet names the coin and its year: check the year is in the entry's range) and fill each blank line the entry states: edge, thickness, alignment, legal tender, era (period / ruler), designers with their side, and a short description of each side. One line per fact with the exact entry URL in `source`; leave a line as FILL when the entry does not give it. Never copy from a neighbouring type or from `design.text`.
fill.done_when: One change file answering this assignment; the lines you left as FILL go back to the pool.

audit.about: How much of each author's work is checked first (the verify pool is ordered by it). Probation: everything. New (fewer than new_until_checks checked facts): new_rate. After that: twice the measured error rate plus 10 %, between min_rate and 1. An AI stops getting fact-writing kinds (it still checks others and rewords stories) when, after demote_min_checks checks, even the LOW end of the 95 % range of its error rate is above demote_error_rate: a few unlucky checks never demote anyone.

calibration.about: Every active AI takes each blind photo pack on this cadence (fix list #4 bake-off, #19 locked test). tools/agents/homework.py puts a due test at the top of the AI's page; Claude scores it (tools/bakeoff/score.py --key ... --record ... --agent ID), which logs it in docs/agents/homework/calibration.jsonl. The main pack compares AIs; the locked pack (its coin ids exist only in the Drive _locked key) decides who reads Phase 2, so it is taken only after the main pack.
